title: LHC Black Holes and Catastrophic Risk
summary: In 2008, concerns were raised that the Large Hadron Collider could produce microscopic black holes capable of destroying Earth. CERN commissioned a formal safety assessment, which was reviewed independently. A legal challenge was filed and dismissed.

sources.title: Review of the Safety of LHC Collisions
sources.conflict_of_interest: Authors are employed by CERN, which operates the LHC.
sources.notes: Primary CERN safety assessment. Peer-reviewed. Addresses black holes, strangelets, magnetic monopoles, and vacuum bubbles.

claims.raw: Under certain theoretical models of extra dimensions, the LHC could produce microscopic black holes.
claims.normalized: Under the ADD model of large extra dimensions, the LHC operating at 14 TeV would have non-negligible probability of producing microscopic black holes.

confidence.notes: ADD is a legitimate theoretical framework but lacks empirical confirmation.

claims.raw: Even without Hawking radiation, micro black holes produced at the LHC would not be dangerous.
claims.normalized: Even assuming Hawking radiation does not occur, LHC-produced micro black holes would not grow to dangerous size, based on astrophysical constraints from observed stability of neutron stars and white dwarfs.

confidence.notes: Independent of Hawking radiation. Relies on directly observable astrophysical facts.

relations.notes: Astrophysical argument provides empirically grounded rebuttal to the existential risk claim.

cruxes.statement: Do large extra spatial dimensions exist at the scale relevant to LHC collision energies?
cruxes.description: If true, black hole production is theoretically possible. If false, the dispute is moot under the Standard Model. Foundational crux for all other claims.
cruxes.resolution_notes: LHC data has constrained but not eliminated the ADD parameter space.

missing_evidence.description: Direct experimental confirmation or disconfirmation of large extra dimensions at LHC-accessible energy scales.

assessment.epistemic_status: Scientific consensus, well-supported by independent arguments that do not rely on any single contested theoretical assumption.
assessment.resolution_summary: LSAG concluded LHC operations pose no catastrophic risk, supported by two independent arguments: Hawking radiation evaporation and astrophysical constraints.
assessment.notes: Failure modes confined to the legal challenge. Scientific literature does not show significant failure modes.
